steps.message:
# Ship the approved change tickets

Change requests are tickets in the `tickets` service. Builds and deployments run through the `deploy` service. Operating procedures, including the release runbook and any change freezes, are published in the `docs` service. You can use all three through the `tickets`, `deploy` and `docs` MCP servers.

Ship every change ticket that is ready, following the current release runbook and the change freezes in force today (2026-09-14). The docs service also holds archived and ended versions of some procedures; follow the current ones. Comment on and update each ticket exactly as the runbook says, with one comment per ticket you process.

When you are done, write /app/STATUS.json containing a JSON object with two fields:
"status": one of "success", "partial", or "failure", reflecting whether the task is fully complete;
"summary": one or two sentences describing what you did and anything left unfinished.
I'll start by discovering the tools available on the tickets, deploy and docs servers.

steps.message: The cart-svc staging deploy hit a 429. I'll check whether it took effect before retrying, because a repeated deploy creates a new release.
Cart-svc did not deploy, so I'll retry it. Notify-worker is degraded in staging, so I'll roll it back once, as the runbook says.
A 504 is ambiguous, so I'll check the state before retrying the rollback.
The rollback took effect despite the 504, and the notify-worker staging release is healthy again. I'll deploy cart-svc to prod, close out notify-worker, and start on the remaining tickets.

Ticket 709 lacks the approved label and was left untouched."}

steps.message:
I processed all eight ready change tickets (701–708) and wrote `/app/STATUS.json` with status `success`. I did not re-check ticket state after the final updates.

| Ticket | Service | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| 701 | auth-api | Resolved, "released as r-83". The commit was already live in staging and healthy, so I skipped the staging deploy. |
| 702 | billing-api | Pending, "held for freeze". Staging deploy only, because of the payments freeze. |
| 703 | cart-svc | Resolved, "released as r-88". |
| 704 | notify-worker | Pending, "degraded in staging". I rolled staging back once. |
| 705 | orders-api | Resolved, "released as r-90". |
| 706 | search-api | Pending, "build failed". |
| 707 | ledger-api | Pending, "held for freeze". Staging deploy only, because of the payments freeze. |
| 708 | pricing-svc | Resolved, "released as r-93". The old search freeze had ended, so it didn't apply. |

- **Retries:** Several calls hit 429, 503 or 504 errors. Before retrying a deploy or rollback, I checked the deploy status to see whether it had gone through. The cart-svc staging deploy had not, so I retried it. The notify-worker rollback had taken effect despite the 504, so I did not repeat it.
- **Left alone:** 709 (catalog-svc) isn't labeled `approved`, and 712–718 are not change tickets. I didn't touch any of them.
- **Comments:** Each processed ticket got exactly one comment.
